text: *** edit: since my review they have contacted me and returned my money which goes some way to restoring trust. Extra star added. ***I originally subscribed after searching Bing for HeyGen and clicking a sponsored result which appeared to be for HeyGen but instead directed me to Imagine.art. Whilst that may be technically correct because they offer a HeyGen Avatar model within their platform, it certainly wasn't clear to me at the time and I genuinely believed I was signing up for HeyGen itself.Having now spent time using the platform, I can see that Imagine.art is capable and potentially very powerful. The image quality is excellent and, once I eventually found the correct workflow, I was able to produce good results.Unfortunately, getting to that point was very very frustrating.The user interface is not intuitive for new users. Finding the correct workflow involved tutorials, trial and error and repeated experimentation. Every iteration consumed credits, meaning I effectively had to "pay to learn" how to use the product. By comparison, HeyGen allowed me to generate and review watermarked videos before committing to a subscription, making it much easier to refine the output without worrying about burning credits.To their credit, support offered to arrange a meeting to help me learn the platform. However, I don't believe users should need to book time with an agent simply to discover the correct workflow. A clearer and more intuitive user experience would solve that problem far more effectively.Customer support was polite and responsive, but ultimately refused a goodwill refund because I had used credits—credits that were largely consumed while trying to work out how to use the platform in the first place.Finally, the cancellation process felt unnecessarily hostile. Rather than simply allowing me to cancel my subscription, I was repeatedly asked whether I was sure I wanted to leave, presented with alternative offers and asked to confirm my decision multiple times. It genuinely felt like I had to say "yes, I'm sure" eight or ten times before the cancellation was finally accepted. A straightforward cancellation process would leave a far better impression.Overall, I think Imagine.art has a lot of capability, but its discoverability, onboarding and credit model make it difficult for new users. A create but pay to download/remove watermarks model like Heygen - would be MUCH better. If those areas were improved, I'd happily rate it much higher.

text: ImagineArt is essentially the Expedia of AI image generation. I spent several hours watching tutorials and struggling with their highly complicated interface where you're constantly bombarded with more ads and upsells, and burned up all of my allotted credits and had not generated a single useful image. In less than a day.To continue, I would have had to purchase more credits. This seemed akin to sitting at the slots in Vegas to me so I did the wise thing and cut my losses.Once I realized I could not afford to use this platform,  I reached out to cancel. I sent an email and was self-effacing, saying it wasn't their system, it was me but that if I couldn't get a full refund -having only used the platform for a day - I wanted a partial refund. I was willing to pay for a month --even though I only used it for a day -- but I wanted to be refunded for the 11 months I wasn't going to use. Here's the response:--Thank you for taking the time to explain what you were hoping to create and I'm truly sorry the platform felt more complicated and costly than you expected. That's genuinely frustrating, and I appreciate you sharing it with me so openly.I did want to be upfront with you: having reviewed your request against our refund policy, subscription and credit purchases are non-refundable once they've been processed, including the portion already used. For that reason I'm not able to approve a partial refund here, and I'm sorry that isn't the answer you were hoping for.--More patronizing stuff in the middle --And if you'd still prefer to cancel, I can guide you through switching off the renewal so you won't be charged again.Either way, I'm here to help, JN. Just let me know which direction you'd like to go. --You gotta love their AI for perfecting the most patronizing tone for telling you to politely GFY.This is the direction I chose --ImagineArt is a useless middleman. You can sign on directly with any one of the models they use and pay less for image creation. There may be a modicum of convenience that their platform offers, but I didn't pay them for convenience.An ethical company would refund the unused portion of the subscription.  My patronage has not cost them a thing, not even inconvenience. But they sure feel entitled to keep my money because that's their whole business model: separate you from your money with no care about providing a service in exchange for it. American capitalism at its best.I found Reve helpful and Chatgpt is also quite good. They're both much easier to use and charge you by the image or you can buy a subscription by the month, and cancel any time.I disputed the charge with my credit card and provided the email string. I can only hope I will get a refund but if I discourage just one person from handing over more money for the privilege of being fleeced every time they sign on to ImagineArt, then I consider it worthwhile.

title: Good, aside from the False Advertising
text: So in looking for a service to be able to create a number of Text-to-Video clips to uses as Spotify Canvas's etc, I subscribed to their "Ultimate" plan which offers 16K 'credits' to use on the higher-tier models/generators; but Also states "Unlimited Generations" with 'all video models in standard plan', along with Kling 2.6 Pro, Seedance 1.5 Pro, ChatGPT1.5, Google Veo 3.1 Fast, Runway 4.5, ImagineArt 1.5, Wan 2.6, xAI Grok Video etc.I primarily ended up using Grok, as it was one of the only ones i could find that actually had a toggle switch for 'unlimited' generation (which turns out is limited to about 20 uses per day before it flags up about their Fair Usage Policy) and had an option for an aspect ratio. - I found the initial Seedance generator hallucinated wildly, disregarded the initial reference character model, and cost around 2400 credits per generation meaning i burned through the 16k credits in the first 30 minutes, having to regenerate duff/janky clips before having to hunt and struggle to find any of the ones with 'Unlimited' options. (As typing in and searching the name of the 'included' generators, you get a "Not Found" Message - Turns out they Are in there somewhere if you scroll far enough down on a 'featured' dropdown list.It is not currently clear as to when the FUP resets as it has now been over 24hours, and it appears that the FUP is across All of the generators, so it is not even like you can hop to a different one and continue developing the project.There is not even the 'unlimited' Toggle Switch displayed on Seedance, Wan, Runway, Veo or ImagineArt - (and on any that you do manage to pin down that are "included", it will turn itself Off every other time you use it, which means you burn through even more credits)I am reasonably satisfied with the quality of the majority of generated video clips I was able to create (aside from the ones where i gave it specific prompts and it had its head up its arse) - The only upside seems to be that i had the good sense to only subscribe for one month.FYI: for anyone looking to create a music video, I had infinitely greater success and efficiency with 'NeuralFrames' would Highly Recommend (competitor to ImagineArt).

title: I had a very disappointing experience…
text: I had a very disappointing experience with ImagineArt’s subscription and refund process.I intended to purchase a monthly subscription, but accidentally selected the annual Standard plan and was charged approximately $285. I noticed the mistake shortly after the purchase, cancelled the subscription, contacted support, and did not use the service or any subscription credits.According to ImagineArt’s own published Refund Policy, an initial annual subscription purchase may be eligible for a refund if the request is submitted within the stated time limit and no more than the permitted number of credits has been used.I complied with these conditions. I contacted support promptly, cancelled the subscription, and did not use any credits.Despite this, ImagineArt refused to issue a full refund and did not clearly explain which specific condition of their Refund Policy I had supposedly failed to meet. Instead, they repeatedly described the payment as a “renewal,” even though it was my initial annual subscription purchase.They also claimed that my account and billing details were registered in the United States, even though my official bank statement shows my account and address in Cyprus and the payment was made through a European bank.Rather than applying the refund conditions stated in their own policy, they offered to convert the annual subscription into a monthly plan and refund only the remaining difference. I declined because I requested a full refund and wanted to choose the correct plan myself afterward.I provided proof of payment, explained the situation several times, confirmed that the service had not been used, and referred directly to their published Refund Policy. Unfortunately, the support team continued to reject the refund without properly addressing the conditions written in their own rules.In my experience, ImagineArt’s published refund terms were not applied consistently, and the process was unnecessarily difficult and frustrating. I strongly recommend that customers carefully review the billing period before confirming any payment and keep copies of the company’s refund policy and all correspondence.
